scores.breakdown:
Rubric: story 25 / problem 15 / solution and architecture 20 / claims 20 / energy and craft 15 / build 5. Score: 22 / 14 / 17 / 17 / 12 / 4.

STORY (22): Fully retellable with no narration. One cursor doubts. Opus 4.5 ships. MONTH 1 to 5 gates lead to a budget. The pull-back shows code was 1 of 7 stations (16%). Work piles up downstream ('the line waits'). 'just add more agents' turns into a swarm (×17.2) and a jam. 'who runs the line?' Lights on, the line runs, the factory appears (graph, hierarchy, swarm, ×4.4), and the foreman is Opus 5.5 with 4 proofs. The button is MONTH 0 to MONTH 1 plus a labelled 2027 projection. The cold-open line 'THE LAST WAVE TOOK ≈5 MONTHS / THE NEXT ONE?' is the best hook of the three.
- Weakness: the structure (the 'what') is explained after the 'who' question, so Act III crams lights-on, the factory, three structure types, ×4.4, the mirror tour, the reveal, 4 proofs and the peak into 32 s.

PROBLEM (14): The most visceral by far, because it shows the mechanism. Cards blast out of the code station at agent speed and slam into dark REVIEW (#36-38). The REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY towers escalate, a progress bar sticks at 97%, 'blocked on review.' appears, and a human is dwarfed under a 300u tower. The naive fix is typed by the human ('just add more agents.'), so the failure is earned. Act II is 38 s (28% of runtime) and runs a little long.

SOLUTION / ARCHITECTURE (17): Shown best of the three, not told:
- #52: two orbs grab one card and it cracks red.
- #88-89: the swarm fans out to read and converges on one writer, who stamps the change.
- #54: a lock-gate jam where 2-3 of 20 orbs get through (the Cursor finding, as pure image).
- #53 to #90: 17 red tendrils, then the coordinator mirror.
The refrain THE LINE WAITS. to THE LINE RUNS., plus 6 true mirror shots, makes the answer feel inevitable. Problems:
- The coordinator node is clay, the hero colour, which implies Google's 4.4× result is Claude's.
- The 'error heals' chime oversells it: 4.4× is still amplification.

CLAIMS (17): The most disciplined treatment on risk.
- It deliberately declines to claim that 'the next wave has started' and asks instead.
- It excludes the SaaSpocalypse.
- It tags ANTHROPIC-REPORTED, SYSTEM CARD and so on.
- The 16% is drawn honestly as a proportional light bar.
Flaws:
- 'SELF-ORGANIZED' strengthens 'picked their own structure'.
- The end card 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.' drops 'with' and 'human'.
- The foreman's 'thousands of amber threads' implies one model directing thousands.
- The greeked newsprint drops the strongest real wave-one evidence (Karpathy's flip, WSJ).

ENERGY / CRAFT (12): It answers the client's 'too slow' complaint best.
- Opus 4.5 arrives at 0:14.5 and Act I ASL is 1.2 s.
- Two accelerando flurries; the peak sits at 85-88%.
- 3 braams and 3 silences; light comes before sound on the reveal.
- The human silhouette is a real emotional anchor.
Weaknesses:
- Proof cards hold for only 1.6-2.0 s, below the hold formula for 25-35 characters.
- Act III ASL of 0.74 just misses the < 0.6 × Act I rule.

BUILD (4): The 4,096-instance cursor city in #31 is over the 2,000-instance budget, and the tempo return to 120 BPM needs a clean splice. Everything else is kit primitives.

Rubric: story 25 / problem 15 / solution and architecture 20 / claims 20 / energy and craft 15 / build 5. Score: 23 / 10 / 16 / 18 / 9 / 5.

STORY (23): The cleanest causal chain of the three, and the easiest to retell. Doubt, then Opus 4.5. The +5/+8/+19 WEEK gates lead to a BUDGET LINE. The pull-back shows 16%. 'MORE AGENTS?' brings the swarm and ×17.2. The coordinator brings ×4.4, then graph, hierarchy and swarm. THE SOFTWARE FACTORY is built but left UNPOWERED, which makes 'who runs the line?' a precise question that the conductor answers by lighting the line. The single cursor motif is elegant and native to this audience: blink, then clay, then a city, a swarm, the conductor, and finally 'stays ON'. Its match cuts on the rectangle are the best motif work in the set.

PROBLEM (10): The weakest link. The '84%' is a dark wall plus a question card, and nothing shows WHY faster code makes the line worse. Act I spends ~14 s on 'human-speed backlog' slabs and ticket walls before agents exist. That muddies which problem we are talking about, and the 16% midpoint then has to re-establish it.

SOLUTION / ARCHITECTURE (16): The architecture is shown well:
- #55: two cursors write the same line and collide.
- #69: parallel read lanes with one clay writer lane.
- 'Unpowered factory, then the conductor lights it' makes Opus 5.5 feel necessary, not decorative.
Problems:
- At #62 the HERO cursor becomes the coordinator that produces Google's 4.4×. That attributes an independent study result to Claude.
- Only ~1 true problem-to-solution mirror (the REVIEW wall becoming a glass gate). It fails the 4-mirror rule.

CLAIMS (18): The most faithful to facts.md.
- The weeks are exact, with real quotes (Karpathy's flip, 'claude-pilled' · WSJ).
- No superlatives. Proof visuals use literal counts (12, 40, 100 to 12 clusters then flat, 6 lanes).
- Vendor tags are kept and the projection is labelled.
Minor issues:
- 'THE OTHER 84%?' is mapped onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL stations, but Atlassian's remainder includes meetings.
- The run-rate is drawn as a column of cursors, which implies coding-only revenue.
- The 6-word proof cards are in ALL CAPS.

ENERGY / CRAFT (9): It repeats the exact sin the client rejected.
- Act I runs 24 s at 1.7 s ASL, with Opus 4.5 not arriving until 0:26.
- #13-19 restate 'human speed' 6 times.
- #42-47 are a victory lap with no new information.
- Act III ASL is 0.91 s, above range, and the Fable/cost card is split into two 1.2 s halves.
On the plus side: the peak at 87%, the final 'cursor stays ON' button and the 2.4 s proof holds are excellent.

BUILD (5): Fully within budget, with explicit particle and instance planning.

Rubric: story 25 / problem 15 / solution and architecture 20 / claims 20 / energy and craft 15 / build 5. Score: 18 / 8 / 12 / 12 / 13 / 3.

STORY (18): It has the most 'movie' twist of the three: a ridge planted three times, then 'that's not the horizon.', revealed as the next wave. The tsunami draw-back makes a beautiful quiet midpoint. But the core metaphor fights the argument. The first wave floods the city, then the water 'drains back' and 84% of the lamps go dark. An exec will read that as 'coding agents receded or failed', which contradicts the film's own run-rate and its Google 75% card. The retell becomes 'did wave one fail?' instead of 'code is only 16% of the job'.

PROBLEM (8): Too thin. The 84% gets about 6 s of labelled dark towers, there is no pile-up mechanism, and the whole problem act is 24 s. The swarm and ×17.2 beats are fine but generic.

SOLUTION / ARCHITECTURE (12): Structure is a lattice inside a particle wall, which is abstract.
- 'One writer per change' appears only in a 0.5 s shot (#69).
- 'Lanes never cross' (#67) is not the same idea.
- At ×4.4 the red pinpoints turn ivory (#68), implying errors vanish.
- 'OPUS 5.5' is shown at 93.6 s, which dilutes the title drop.

CLAIMS (12): The most hype risk.
- 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' states the client's framing as fact.
- 'THE WHOLE LINE.' (#110) claims end-to-end delivery that no fact supports.
- '~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE' is shown as a log zoom into the factory wave. It is an Anthropic-internal number from before Opus 5.5 and it is not a structured factory.
- Google's 75% is laid over the Claude spark's wave, implying it is Claude's work.
- A 50× wall of water is a magnitude claim made in pictures.

TONE: A giant wave breaking over a city of desks with tiny people at them is disaster/job-loss imagery, and the climax repeats it (#107). It would embarrass the sender in front of an exec audience.

ENERGY / CRAFT (13): Grand and fast; Opus 4.5 arrives at 0:16. The type-as-architecture work is the best in the set: numerals built from lit lamps, letters built from lanes. Weaknesses:
- Proof cards hold for only 1.2-1.6 s.
- 9 flashes.
- Act III ASL is marginal.

BUILD (3): A 30k-particle ocean plus the wave lattice sit at the particle caps, and the planted ridge may not read at phone size.
fatal_flaws: The 16% 'drain-back' (#39-40: 84% of lamps revert to dark) misstates Atlassian's time-share statistic as the first wave's reach or a retreat, and contradicts the adoption facts.
The tsunami-over-a-city-of-desks imagery (#4, #38, #59-61, and the peak at #107 where the factory wave breaks over the lit city) reads as disaster/replacement to an executive audience.
'THE WHOLE LINE.' (#110) and 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' (#61) state capability and framing that facts.md does not support.

steal: signal #27 + #29: wave one's real, week-stamped human proof. Put Karpathy's flip ('…never felt this much behind…' · KARPATHY) as the one legible pane inside machine's MONTH 2 gate, replacing machine #19's greeked newsprint. The doubter from machine #10 then visibly flips 5 weeks later, the strongest credibility beat for this audience. Optionally add ''claude-pilled' · WSJ' at MONTH 3. Pay for the ~6-9 words by cutting the REVIEW./TEST./DEPLOY. recall labels in machine #91-93 (the mirrors read without them) and the 'blocked on review.' pane.

signal #71 + #86: show the factory first as UNLIT wireframe stations, so machine's LIGHTS-ON (#78-81) reads as caused by the model arriving, not as ambient lighting. Structure is necessary; the model powers it.

signal #95-96: the SAME 100 orbs snap into 12 sub-lead clusters, then re-snap flat. Doing it in sequence says 'picked their own structure' (per task) more clearly than machine #99's simultaneous left/right split.
signal #92-94: exact literal counts on the proofs (exactly 12 threads from one session; 40 PR blocks flipping green one per 16th until all are green). Keep these counts exact in machine #101.

signal proof timing: give each proof card ≥2.4 s and run FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK → 40% LOWER COST VS OPUS 5 as one continuous two-stage shot of about 3.2 s (signal #101's two columns: the level line holds while the cost bar shrinks). Machine's 1.6 s holds fail the read-time formula.

signal #115: the final image. The lone cursor blinks on the tick, then STOPS blinking and stays ON with the final sting (the agent no longer waits for a human). Use it as the last beat after machine #123-124's MONTH 0 → MONTH 1 and the projection, instead of the black ring-out in #125.
signal #89: a work card passes the former REVIEW wall, going in ice and coming out clay. A micro-payoff to add to machine's mirror tour.
signal #23: after silence, the cursor fires a horizontal light line that shape-matches the next gate edge. Use it as the match-cut grammar for machine's NOV 24 slab to GATE 1 transition.

machine (keep as the spine) #36-38: cards blast out of the code station at agent speed and slam into dark REVIEW. This is the causal reason coding agents alone are not enough. Keep #30's plant (finished cards shooting off-frame into darkness).
machine (keep) #38/#48 → #82: the refrain THE LINE WAITS. (×2, same slot and font) flipping to THE LINE RUNS. on BRAAM #2 as the letterbox opens.
machine (keep) #35: a light bar sweeps exactly 16% of the line's length and stops. The honest 16% visual, better than any '84%' card.

machine (keep, strengthen) #52 → #89: make the 'two writers grab one card, it cracks red' macro and the 'one writer stamps, card turns green' macro IDENTICAL compositions. Extend #88 to ≥2.0 s so the read fan-out, then the convergence on a single writer, registers. That is 'parallelize reading, one writer per change' shown, not told.
machine (keep, fix) #53 → #90: 17 red tendrils, then in the mirror exactly 4 remain. ×4.4 is still error amplification; the visual must stay honest. Render the coordinator node ivory, not clay.
machine (keep) #54: the lock-gate jam where 20 orbs crowd a gate and only 2-3 pass (the Cursor finding as pure image, no card).
machine (keep) #94-96: stillness, then light BEFORE sound, then the '5.5' engraving fragment on the delayed boom. Keep #123-124 MONTH 0 → MONTH 1 as the clock-restart hook.

wave #44 → #102: the tick as a speed comparison. A steel cursor at the REVIEW station blinks every 2 beats (human speed) while the clay spark streaks past, and in the Act III mirror it blinks every beat in clay. Drop it into machine's Act II/III REVIEW compositions.
wave #69: the read-beam iconography. Many agents cast thin read-beams onto one slab while one draws the single write line. Use it as the visual grammar for machine #88.
wave #29 / #40: type as architecture. Build machine's '≈5 MONTHS' / '16%' numerals from the lit elements in the world (lamps or orbs) rather than overlaying them.

wave #8 / #11 / #31: planting. In machine's Act I hall wides (#9, #11), let dark station silhouettes sit half-seen in the fog, so the midpoint pull-back (#34) pays off a plant ('those weren't pillars, they were stations').

NEW (from the end-credit fact): replace machine #98's human dwarfed at the obelisk's foot. Put the human silhouette at the HEAD of the line handing a single light-card brief to the foreman. That pays off 'MADE WITH OPUS 5.5 AGENTS / FROM ONE HUMAN BRIEF' and removes the worship/replacement reading.
cut: wave #39-40: the drain-back where 84% of lamps go dark. It misrepresents the 16% time-share statistic and implies wave one receded.

wave tsunami imagery overall: #4, #38 (the wave breaking over the city of desks), #59-61 and the peak at #107 (the factory wave breaking over the lit city). It reads as disaster or job loss to an exec audience.
wave #110 'THE WHOLE LINE.': no fact shows Opus 5.5 running review, test, deploy and operate end to end.
wave #61 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' and the 50× wave scale. These state client framing as fact or magnitude. Keep machine's question 'THE NEXT ONE?' plus the labelled projection.
wave #72 '~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE' as a log zoom into the factory wave. It conflates an Anthropic-internal, pre-5.5 number with structure and with Opus 5.5.
wave #31 'GOOGLE 75%' laid over the Claude spark's wave. Implied attribution, and it isn't needed.
wave #68: red pinpoints turning ivory at ×4.4 (implies errors are eliminated).
wave #86: the 'OPUS 5.5' card at 93.6 s, which dilutes the title drop.
machine #99 'SELF-ORGANIZED': use the verbatim 'PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE' (set 5-7-word cards in sentence case).
machine #126 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.': use 'Made with Claude Opus 5.5 agents / from one human brief.'
machine #98: 'thousands of amber threads' (implies one model directing thousands; the facts top out at 100-agent teams and a dozen sessions). Draw threads to the 8 stations or 12 sub-leads.

machine #90 'error heals' chime and signal #62 'red drains': don't imply zero errors. Also cut the CLAY/hero-coloured coordinator on the Google 4.4× result (machine #90, signal #62, where the hero cursor becomes the coordinator). The study isn't about Claude.
machine #19: the greeked newsprint panes (replace with the legible Karpathy flip).
machine #31: the 4,096-instance cursor city. It is redundant and over the 2,000-instance engine budget.
signal #13-19: ~7 s of repeated 'human-speed' padding before Opus 4.5. It is exactly the slowness the client rejected.
signal #42-47: the victory-lap filler (station exterior, lanes, orbit), with no new information.

'THE OTHER 84%?' card (signal #51, wave #44) and any mapping of the 84% onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL as a claim. Atlassian's remainder includes meetings; let the dark 84% of machine #35's bar speak as illustration.

Run-rate column built from cursors, orbs or desk lamps at the code station (signal #36, machine #25, wave #24). It implies coding-only revenue; render a neutral column and keep ANTHROPIC-REPORTED at least 22 px.

Any declarative 'the next wave has started'. facts.md supports only a labelled projection. If the client insists, the only safe on-screen support is Shapiro's 'a handful of teams so far'. Never use StrongDM's 'not reviewed by humans', and never use competitor raises (Factory $5B, Kiro).
Sub-2.0 s proof-card holds (machine #102/#104/#105 at 1.6 s, wave #96-97 at 1.2 s, signal #101's 1.2 s split). They fail the read-time formula on phones.
fact_problems: machine #99: '100-AGENT TEAMS, SELF-ORGANIZED' slightly strengthens the system card's 'picked their own structure'.
machine #126: 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.' strengthens 'researched… rendered WITH Claude Opus 5.5 agents, from one HUMAN brief' and implies no human role.
machine #98: 'thousands of amber threads' from the foreman implies Opus 5.5 directs thousands of agents. The facts are a dozen sessions (Stripe) and 100-agent teams.
machine #90 and signal #62: the Google Research coordinator result (17.2× → 4.4×) is drawn as the clay/hero Claude element, which misattributes an independent study to the product.
machine #90 ('error heals' chime), signal #62 ('red drains') and wave #68 (red → ivory): 4.4× is still error amplification. Visuals must not imply errors vanish.

wave #39-40: 16% is the share of developer TIME spent writing code (Atlassian), not the share of desks or work the wave reached. The drain-back implies adoption receded, against Google's 75% and JetBrains' 18% → ~39%.
wave #72: '~30,000 agents at once' is Anthropic-internal (Aug 2026, before Opus 5.5) and says nothing about structure. Zooming from one spark into the factory wave conflates both.
wave #31: Google's 75% AI-generated code is not Claude's output, but it is shown over the Claude spark's wave.
wave #110 'THE WHOLE LINE.': unsupported. The facts show multi-repo runs, stacked PRs green in CI and 18+ hours unattended, not end-to-end delivery.
wave #61 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.': the client thesis is stated as fact. facts.md supports only 'If the pattern holds: budgets in early 2027' as a labelled projection.
signal #49/#51 and wave #44: 'THE OTHER 84%?' laid onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL. Atlassian's remaining 84% includes meetings and non-delivery time (signal flags this itself).
signal #36, machine #25 and wave #24: the ~$9B → $30B+ run-rate is company-wide and Anthropic-reported, but each visual builds it from coding cursors, orbs or lamps, implying coding-only revenue.

machine #14-24: the MONTH 1 to 5 gates are schematic. The facts are +5/+8/+19 weeks, and the run-rate lands at about month 4.4. This is fine under '≈5 months', but signal's week stamps are the exact form.
All three: the same clay protagonist plays Opus 4.5 (wave one) and Opus 5.5 (the conductor or foreman). A grade or form change is needed so viewers don't read the 4.5-era results as 5.5's.
